open_obligations: Check whether the union ceiling is attainable by any single model or only an oracle combination.
Check which models and datasets Goel et al.'s ceiling estimates cover and how they compare with Burns et al.'s setting.
Check how much PGR values would change under the alternative ceiling.
Check that the 'Ground-truth Elicitation (previous)' ceiling is computed as Burns et al.'s strong ceiling; Goel et al. describe that upper bound as training the strong student on ground-truth labels.
out.other_title: Performance gap recovered (PGR) metric for weak-to-strong generalization
out.rationale: Burns et al. define PGR as the fraction of the performance gap between the weak and strong ceiling models that is recovered with weak supervision. Goel et al. say PGR normalises the gain over the weak supervisor by an 'upper-bound' obtained by training the strong student on ground-truth labels, and that leveraging complementary knowledge effectively might actually allow Sw2s > Sgt, questioning that upper bound. They report a ceiling estimate of +14.1 for their Elicitation ∪ Complementary estimate versus +11.2 for the previous ground-truth elicitation estimate; the cited passages do not show whether this higher estimate is achievable.
out.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether the strong ceiling in PGR's denominator is an upper bound on weak-to-strong performance, which Goel et al. question with a higher ceiling estimate that counts the weak supervisor's complementary knowledge
